details: Legacy flagship finding. The direction (pathological hyper-coupling, not disconnection) is the key surprise differentiating this from standard decoupling theory. Quarantined: legacy-reported, not re-executed in this registry.
signal: Awake glucose-HR correlation moves from -0.041 (healthy) to +0.045 (insulin-dependent), monotonic, d=0.585, FDR=1.3e-19 (legacy H-MIG01).
summary: Diabetes increases glucose-HR coupling (hyper-coupling) rather than decoupling it — opposite to the classical network-physiology decoupling narrative.

details: Implies the broadband glucose-HR increase in H-MIG01 is driven entirely by slow (>2h) coupling while fast coupling actually breaks down — consistent with early parasympathetic/vagal denervation. Partially contradicts the broadband framing of H-MIG01. Quarantined: legacy-reported (Welch coherence, not full CWT), not re-executed; >8h band and <30min control unreliable.
signal: Legacy H-NEW01: 30-60min d=-0.22, 1-2h d=-0.17, 2-4h d=+0.33, 4-8h d=+0.38 (FDR p=1e-8); broadband n.s.
summary: Glucose-HR coupling sign-flips by timescale: fast (30min-2h) coherence DECREASES with diabetes severity while slow (2-8h) coherence INCREASES; broadband effect (d=0.06) is non-significant.
